entries.proposition: In a four-compound pilot screen, ethosuximide was the only compound that restored the chemotaxis defect of the knock-in worms to wild-type level; rolipram and two iron chelators did not. The screen compared treated mutants with wild-type N2 controls that were not treated: this paper has no wild-type plus ethosuximide arm.
entries.snippet: The initial screen, carried out on dnj-14(L116Δ) ANCL mutants, revealed ethosuximide as the only compound able to rescue the chemotaxis defect to the levels of the wild-type N2 controls (Fig. 5A).
entries.anchor: Results, Screen for compounds that rescue ANCL dnj-14 mutants identifies ethosuximide

entries.proposition: Ethosuximide also rescued heterozygous mutant worms (one wild-type and one mutant copy), the genotype that mimics the patients; the effect was against a vehicle control in the same genotype.
entries.snippet: Similarly, we found that both heterozygous ANCL mutant worms had significant improvement in chemotaxis when grown under the presence of ethosuximide, compared with that of the vehicle control, DMSO (Fig. 5C).
entries.anchor: Results, Screen for compounds that rescue ANCL dnj-14 mutants identifies ethosuximide

entries.proposition: A statement that the cited earlier work found no significant effect of ethosuximide and rolipram on wild-type worms, which would make the rescue genotype-restricted in worms; this paper does not itself show that arm, and the reference is cited, not read here.
entries.snippet: Ethosuximide and rolipram were selected as they have previously been reported to rescue the lifespan and chemotaxis phenotype of other dnj-14 mutant alleles but had no significant effect on wild-type worms (26,27).
entries.anchor: Results, Screen for compounds that rescue ANCL dnj-14 mutants identifies ethosuximide

entries.proposition: Mechanism: the rescue also happens in null worms that have no protein, so it is not a correction of the mutant protein; the authors think it acts through a distinct pathway downstream of the transcription factor DAF-16/FOXO acting in parallel to the protein's neuroprotective function, based on previous findings, and say the precise mechanism is unknown. No T-type channel is invoked and none was tested.
entries.snippet: Hence, it seems most probable that the rescuing effect of the drug comes from the activation of a distinct pathway(s) that acts in parallel to CSP’s neuroprotective mechanism(s).

entries.proposition: Authors' caveats: the lack of an effect of iron chelators and rolipram should not be read as evidence against them (one concentration, cuticle penetration, dominant-negative versus null mechanism); and the palmitoylation or aggregation state of the worm protein could not be tested.
entries.snippet: However, it is important to stress that the lack of effect seen in this study should not be interpreted as evidence against the proposed therapeutic use of iron chelators for ANCL patients.

entries.proposition: Figure 5 read as an image (the bucket jpg): panels A and B show cumulative percentage of worms on the food spot over 120 min; the ethosuximide curve for both homozygous knock-ins climbs to about 95 percent, close to the wild-type N2 curve and well above the vehicle curves (about 62 and 75 percent at 120 min); rolipram and the iron chelators sit with or below the vehicle curves. Panel C: heterozygous worms with vehicle reach about 65 and 45 percent and with ethosuximide about 95 and 90 percent. There is no wild-type N2 plus ethosuximide curve in any panel.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 5A and 5B: N2 black curve about 93 to 99 percent at 120 min; ethosuximide curves about 95 to 98; DMSO curves about 62 to 75; Figure 5C: ethosuximide dashed curves about 90 to 95 versus DMSO solid curves about 44 to 65.
